sources.name: RIVERBOOK › Edited Drafts (and its Script tabs)

notes: The timeline sheet is canon for years and family; the Edited Drafts tab is canon for the stories.
Ages of the Sultan and the princes come from the character designs, not from canon.
Portraits are the starred cast sheets of the "Riverbanks house style", copied in on each sync.
Jalal's and Shapla's birth years (2031, 2033) were invented on 2026-10-02 to fill gaps in canon.

people.name: Ismahan
people.summary: Youngest child of Sultan Nuh of Mua. At 18 she is the youngest delegate at the 2028 Sunda Summit; in 2030 she becomes the first leader of the consensus-based kinship councils as the sultanate gives way to a pluriversal matriarchy. On sabbatical in 2052 she is Ya's boatmate on a KAN sailabout. Grandmother of Teja.

people.name: Sultan Nuh
people.summary: Ageing Sultan of Mua (around seventy in 2027), sceptical of the Sunda Summit as another Western scheme. Sends his youngest instead of his sons, and in 2030 signs the Confluence Accord.

people.name: Tengku Hamzah
people.summary: The General: elder prince and commander of Mua's military. Promises his troops can handle any disaster; in the 2029 crisis the fishers and farmers carry his soldiers while he takes the credit. Humbled.

people.name: Tengku Faris
people.summary: The Financier: second prince, years on Wall Street. His lines of credit fail in the 2029 crisis while PREMISE derivatives pay out to those most in need without him. Humbled.

people.name: Soraya
people.summary: Ismahan's daughter, the middle generation, and Teja's mother.

people.name: Teja
people.summary: Soraya's daughter and Ismahan's granddaughter. Appears at 11 in a scene with Grandma Ismahan (2075).

people.name: Dew
people.summary: Runs the family's Chinese restaurant on stilts on the Ping; her cooking lived by the Gross Delish Index before it had a name. At the 2028 Sunda Summit with the Ping river valley delegation she shares a meal with young Ismahan. Teaches eight-year-old Ya to cook through the year it snowed (2040) and dies the next year; her shrine sits under the restaurant, reachable when the water drops.

people.name: Ya
people.summary: Dew's granddaughter, from a Chinese immigrant family long settled on the Ping, with a fluid sense of home. Learns to cook from Dew in 2040; on her 2052 sailabout teaches Ismahan to cook. Inspired by that trip into research; by 2065 she studies food ecosystems with the Bengal Passage Cooperative and recruits Jalal.

people.name: Taro
people.summary: Ya's grey tabby: a tiny kitten on the 2052 sailabout, a teenage cat (cats live longer now) at her side in 2065.

people.name: Jalal
people.summary: Meghna fisherman whose second-hand drone nets a research-tagged hilsa. His metis cracks Ya's data puzzle (the hilsa have gone home up the old channel); in 2065 he decides to become a data collector and follow the hilsa.

people.name: Shapla
people.summary: Jalal's wife. Her family's history is one of leaving: Bengal after Partition, then the drowned delta. She cooks the tagged hilsa into the feast.

people.name: The drone
people.summary: A chatty second-hand fishing drone Jalal bought at a night market. Formerly KAN's, so KAN researchers can still patch in through it.

people.name: KAN
people.summary: The adaptation network. Runs sailabouts (Young Leaders, Executive MBA) and the research network the Bengal Passage Cooperative belongs to.

people.name: Bengal Passage Cooperative
people.summary: Research organisation in the KAN network helping the fishers and farmers of the river system; tracks tagged hilsa.
